notes: A dash '-' in the chart means the rating does not apply; it is recorded as null. No cells were truly blank.
'*' after CPA: the unit keeps that CPA whatever the CPA of the TOE Strength Points assigned to it.
'+' after CPA: the unit historically had enough trucks to motorize fully; if motorized only its CPA changes.

Parentheses around a rating, e.g. (1): the unit may not use that rating if any unit in the hex has ammo and a non-parenthesized number for that rating; Replacement Points do not stop it using the rating.
'†' on CW max TOE 10 (code g): if the unit is all US tank TOE Strength Points, its maximum is nine.
Max TOE may be exceeded only by the unit's arrival/deployment TOE strength.
For rows with a may-assign note, the chart prints '-' on the rating line and the max TOE number on the note line; we record that number as max_toe.
unit_type is carried down from the group label printed on the first row of each group.
SP in assign_note = TOE Strength Points.

CW chart notes: from 1/39 certain recon units may upgrade (Case 20.5); from 1/75 infantry battalions k-t may add anti-tank TOE SP (Case 19.9); from 1/87 infantry battalions n, p, r, s may upgrade (Case 20.77); h and j are non-motorized (may motorize with Truck Points; SAS via CW LDG, Case 27.88).
CW chart is printed twice: scan p132-133 and p166 (second copy, retypeset: 'Tank Bn-Equivalent', max TOE '10**' for g). Values on p166 spot-checked, matched p132; p132-133 used.
Italian close assault ratings like (3)/(2) and 0/(1) are split into offence/defence keeping the parentheses.
Italian kk max TOE printed as '9' over '+3' (nine artillery plus three AA); recorded as '9+3'. Italian pp max TOE printed '8AA'.

Italian notes: from 1/39 'ww' recon may upgrade (Case 20.5); from 1/75 Italian battle groups and some HQs may add anti-tank SP (Case 19.8); vv = Autoblinda 41, ww = Autoblinda 40, both Breakdown Adjustment Rating 1 Left; units with heavy AA SP have 75/46 guns; 't' has armour protection only when carried by truck/motorization points (counts as halftracks, Case 14.88).

German chart printed twice: p136 and p170. They differ only in the mark on HQ c and d CPA: p136 prints '30**', p170 prints '30†'. The key defines '**' (keeps CPA regardless of assigned SP) and no '†', so '30**' is recorded.

German '*' after ID codes b and e (recorded as plain 'b','e'): this HQ may be eligible to add anti-tank TOE SP (Case 19.8). German '**' after CPA: keeps that CPA regardless of the SP assigned. German '‡' on j CPA: when carried by truck/motorization points the unit counts as halftracks (Case 14.88); otherwise it has no armour protection, and motorizing changes more than CPA.
German notes: from 1/39 'ff' recon may upgrade (Case 20.5); from 1/75 German battle groups and some HQs may add anti-tank SP (Case 19.8); ee and ff have Breakdown Adjustment Rating 1 Left.
German dd row prints no dashes at all on its rating line (blank cells); recorded as null like the dashes.
German 'Heavy Anti-air' label prints on the cc row and 'Bn-Eq' on the dd row; both recorded as 'Heavy Anti-air Bn-Eq'.
uncertain: de v close_assault_offence (a lone '*' printed in the Close Assault column, no '/'; meaning unexplained in the key)

Cross-check: read twice, once from the archive.org scan (jp2 132-133, 168-170, 136) and once from the community 300 dpi chart PDFs (Commonwealth Charts.pdf pp. 22-23, Axis Charts.pdf pp. 26-28); 1612 cells compared, 7 differed. Spacing and wording of unit_type and assign_note are ours, not compared.

German c and d CPA: the German chart set (jp2 170) and the Discord scan print 30 with a dagger, which the 4.46c key does not define; the copy on jp2 136 prints 30 with a double asterisk (keeps its CPA whatever is assigned). Recorded as 30† as printed on the chart set; question for the printed copy.
German v close assault: a lone asterisk is printed with no slash; one read put it in both fields. Kept in offence only, defence null; question for the printed copy.
The charts are headed 4.46a/b/c on the chart sets; the ID code of an OA counter (data/oa/) keys into this table by nation.

equivalent is our reading of the unit type for stacking (SPI 9.22-9.24, 9.4): brigade, battalion or company from the type's own name, hq for headquarters (0 SP alone, a company once anything is attached). The German Engineer Bn/Coy-Eq and Commonwealth Construction (Road/RR) rows cover both battalions and companies, so they say by-unit and each OA unit with that code carries its own equivalent, read from its name (Bn, Regt: battalion; Coy, Koy, Bty: company)
